verdict: Strategy lost $8.2B in a single quarter — almost all of it a paper writedown of its Bitcoin stash as the price fell — while the actual software business took in $122M and roughly broke even before the Bitcoin line.

kpis.label: Bitcoin loss
kpis.note: paper writedown — no Bitcoin sold for this loss, no cash out

segments.name: Software revenue
segments.note: The original business: analytics software — subscriptions ($62.9M), product support ($40.2M), licenses ($3.7M) and other services ($15.6M). Up 7% YoY as subscriptions keep replacing licenses.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — for Strategy this also covers the machinery of its Bitcoin treasury strategy.

opex.name: Unrealized Bitcoin loss
opex.note: Strategy holds Bitcoin and marks it to market price every quarter (accounting rule ASU 2023-08). Bitcoin's price fell in Q2, so the stash was written down by $8.3B. This is a paper loss — it reverses if the price recovers — and the filing puts it inside operating expenses.

follow100Note: Shrunk to $100 of software revenue, the Bitcoin writedown is $6,795 — it dwarfs the software business, which is the story of this company.

takeaways.title: A paper loss, not a cash loss
takeaways.text: Bitcoin fell during the quarter, so accounting rules wrote the stash down by $8.3B. Strategy actually bought 85,296 more Bitcoin in Q2 for $6.4B and ended June holding 846,000.

takeaways.title: The software business is steady
takeaways.text: Software revenue grew 7% to $122M with a 67% gross margin — subscriptions ($63M) are now the biggest piece as licenses shrink. Before the Bitcoin line, software gross profit roughly covered running costs.

takeaways.title: Common holders bear it all
takeaways.text: After $401M of dividends on Strategy's preferred stock, the loss attributable to common stockholders was $8.62B, or $24.45 per share.

oneTimers: The $8.3B Bitcoin loss is not a sale — it is a mark-to-market revaluation under accounting rule ASU 2023-08 (in force since January 1, 2025), which runs Bitcoin's price changes through earnings every quarter. It will be back next quarter, as a gain or a loss: over the first half of 2026 this same line nets to a $22.8B loss.
Between net loss and what common shareholders 'got': $400.7M of dividends on Strategy's preferred stock — leaving −$8,620.3M attributable to common stockholders.
Strategy repurchased $1.5B of its 2029 convertible notes for about $1.38B in cash in May 2026, booking a $113.9M gain on debt extinguishment — it sits in other income above.
otherDetail: A $113.9M gain on buying back $1.5B of convertible notes for about $1.38B in cash (an 8% discount to par), plus $0.2M of other income, minus $1.3M of net interest expense.
footerNote: Formerly MicroStrategy. The Bitcoin writedown sits in operating expenses, as filed.
